# Text test font (T-0130, ADR-0033)

`CarvettoTest-Regular.ttf` (1.6 KB) is an original font made for Carvetto's tests. It is not derived
from any other font. It is generated by `tools/make_test_font.py` (standard library only,
byte-reproducible; regenerate with `python3 tools/make_test_font.py`) and licensed under the
SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`OFL.txt`; no Reserved Font Name). The licence is also in the font's
`name` table (IDs 0, 13, 14). It is used only by the unit tests and is not shipped in releases.

Units per em 1000, ascender 800, descender -200, line gap 100 (line height 1100). TrueType
quadratic outlines, outer contours clockwise as in TrueType. Areas below are in font units squared.

| Glyph | Code point | Advance | Shape | Net area |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .notdef | - | 500 | 400x700 box, 200x500 counter | 180000 |
| space | U+0020 | 300 | empty | 0 |
| I | U+0049 | 400 | bar 100..300 x 0..700 | 140000 |
| T | U+0054 | 700 | bar 0..600 x 600..700 on stem 250..350 | 120000 |
| O | U+004F | 800 | rounded square (quadratic curves), rounded counter | 275000 (408333.33 - 133333.33) |
| alef | U+05D0 | 600 | L shape (asymmetric) | 100000 |
| acutecomb | U+0301 | 0 | bar -300..-100 x 750..850 | 20000 |
| Eacute | U+00C9 | 400 | composite: I + acute shifted by 400 | 160000 |

Kerning (legacy `kern` table): T followed by O = -120. No GPOS/GSUB. U+05D0 is a strong
right-to-left character, so it exercises RTL shaping.

## CarvettoTestCFF-Regular.otf (812 bytes)

An OpenType/CFF font (cubic outlines, PostScript-style winding) generated by `tools/make_test_cff.py`,
original Carvetto work under the same OFL 1.1 (`OFL.txt`). Units per em 1000, no kerning.

| Glyph | Code point | Advance | Shape | Net area |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .notdef | - | 500 | empty | 0 |
| A | U+0041 | 700 | box 600x700, 400x500 hole | 420000 - 200000 = 220000 |
| B | U+0042 | 700 | line, cubic (500,0) (800,100) (800,400) (500,500), line | 250000 + 81000 = 331000 |
| C | U+0043 | 1000 | four-cubic circle r500, clockwise hole r200 | about pi (500^2 - 200^2) |
